plants.name: Rosa 'Gertrude Jekyll' and other garden roses (Rosa spp.)
plants.description: Mid-June is peak rose season in temperate Northern Hemisphere gardens. Old English-style roses open in layers of silky, fragrant petals. Their perfume drifts across cottage borders, arbors and walls, and bees crowd the open blooms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late May to July, with the main flush in June
plants.location: Temperate Europe and the United States, including England and the Pacific Northwest
plants.funFact: Fossils show roses have existed for more than 30 million years. That is long before humans began breeding them.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of tiny, fragrant purple flowers. In the sunny Mediterranean hills, the blooms hum with bees and scent the warm air with their clean, herbal fragrance.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to midsummer, with flowering beginning in June in southern Europe
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, especially Provence in southern France
plants.funFact: The name lavender likely comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. Romans used the herb to scent their baths.

plants.name: Telopea speciosissima
plants.description: Waratah flowers are crimson, dome-shaped heads ringed by bold red bracts. Each head is made of hundreds of tiny flowers. Native to the sandstone bushland around Sydney, it is the floral emblem of New South Wales.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring, roughly August to November
plants.funFact: The waratah's nectar-rich flowers are pollinated mainly by honeyeater birds. The name comes from an Aboriginal word meaning 'seen from afar'.
